title: Every runnable README code block executes on the installed wheel from a directory outside the checkout

fixture.marker_rule: a fenced ```python block is runnable in the CPU environment unless the nearest non-blank line above it is <!-- readme-example: cuda --> (runs in the CUDA environment) or <!-- readme-example: skip: reason --> (never runs, reason recorded); blocks in other languages are listed, not executed
fixture.runner: scripts/run_readme_examples.py, called by scripts/clean_install_check.py after both environments exist; blocks run in README order in one working directory <local-root>/tmp/clean_install/work/readme, each in a fresh interpreter process with PYTHONPATH removed and TMP/TEMP under that directory
blocks_on_declaration: python, cuda: the 3D waveguide, 8 x 6 x 2 um at 0.05 um, 1000 steps, backend cuda, cuda_kernel fused; project.save('project.json'), Simulation.run, result.save('results/run.npz')
python, cpu: the 2D default waveguide, backend auto, Simulation.run, result.save('results/first.npz'), Result.load and print of summary['backend']
fixture.interpreter_check: each interpreter must import torchfdtd from its own sys.prefix and not from the checkout before any block runs
fixture.platforms: Windows 11 on this host; Linux NOT_RUN (the same command runs unchanged in WSL: python scripts/clean_install_check.py --local-root <dir> --find-links <wheels> --skip-cuda)

reference_method: the exit code of each block's process; the block text itself is the reference and is hashed into the record so that a changed block invalidates it

observables.name: block_status
observables.definition: per block with its mode, line, SHA-256, interpreter, exit code, duration and output tails

observables.name: runnable_blocks_sha256
observables.definition: digest over the code of every cpu and cuda block in README order

observables.name: interpreter_location
observables.definition: torchfdtd.__file__ and sys.prefix of each interpreter

acceptance.blocks: every cpu block exits 0 in the CPU environment and every cuda block exits 0 in the CUDA environment; at least one block saves a result and one loads it back; skipped blocks carry a reason
acceptance.record: readme_examples.all_runnable_passed true in the newest docs/validation/clean_install record and readme.runnable_blocks_sha256 equal to the digest of the current README
acceptance.isolation: every interpreter's torchfdtd.__file__ lies inside its sys.prefix and outside the checkout
acceptance.source_of_limits: COMPLETION_PROGRAM_KO.md G8-07 (install, first computation, save, load on every advertised platform, from a changed working directory); pass/fail only

not_yet_covered: Linux: the record is Windows only; the Linux column stays NOT_RUN until the same script is run there
macOS: documented for CPU install only, no record
the powershell blocks are not executed by the runner; the clean-install steps exercise the same commands (pip install of the wheel, torchfdtd doctor, torchfdtd serve) individually

notes: Declared on branch g8-packaging from 2b64f91 before the recorded run. The README's first python block requires a CUDA device and the cuda-kernels extra by design (it selects the measured 3D fused path, and tests/test_readme_measurements.py fixes that); it is therefore marked cuda and runs in the CUDA environment, and a second block that runs on any install was added for the CPU environment.
